publicReleaseNotes: Uptime 0.5.8 keeps definition imports and monitor erasure in place while you verify a fresh second factor, then continues the saved request. Erasing a monitor shows the completed receipt, its time and per-table record counts before you close it to return to the monitor list. Actions entered while the security panel is first loading wait for its reads instead of being silently dropped. Newly issued keys show this installation's Read API address, an Authorization: Bearer <YOUR_KEY> example and a guide link; CI keys explain that their scope is definition operations, not monitoring reads. The README leads with the installer command that needs no preinstalled Node, and the monitor and definition guides match the current console, scheduled-job check-in flow and already available ICMP ping option. No migration and no new required settings; the pinned @runeditrun/rer stays at 0.2.108; update an existing checkout with pnpm install --frozen-lockfile. Known issues: heartbeat output saved by 0.5.6 or earlier is not rewritten, so rotate a key earlier output may have contained; pattern-based redaction can still miss an unlabelled secret of no recognizable shape that is not listed under Output text to mask. A monitor CSV exported from UptimeRobot still cannot be imported (the v3 JSON, an event-log CSV and Uptime's own url CSV are read). Restoring an installation archive does not bring back the list of erased people, so a Business that pairs again after a restore and still lists an erased person could invite them again. A company with a signed agent policy but no company settings still receives an empty decision-feed page rather than a refusal (no token or decision is shared). Response bodies over 64 KiB still fail the check; monitor a smaller page such as a health endpoint. Other limits from earlier releases remain. The product screenshot was taken on 0.4.0, before the console changes of 0.5.0 through 0.5.8. Product screenshot: .github/assets/release/uptime-0.4.0-monitor-1440.png
